reconcile.note: Gill resolves the tension by reading Acts 7:16 as compressing two separate purchases, Abraham's Machpelah field and Jacob's Shechem plot, into a single summary reference.

discrepancy.note: Troki charges Stephen's speech with confusing the two patriarchs, assigning Jacob's Shechem purchase to Abraham through mere hearsay.

quotes.text: Fifthly, the plot of field, situated near Schachem, was purchased by Jacob, and not by Abraham. The author of the Acts had but a confused idea of the several purchases made by the patriarchs Abraham and Jacob, and his statements respecting them must have been from hearsay.
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah) (1851), ch. LXIII, on Acts 7:16.

sides.snippet: buried they in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money
sides.verseText: The bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of money: and they became the inheritance of the children of Joseph.

sides.snippet: and they were brought back to Shechem, and laid in the tomb that Abraham bought for a price in silver from the children of Hamor of Shechem.
